I'm putting together some custom CSS for my subs, and I'm fairly new to CSS. How can I detect when a user is using night mode, and apply different CSS values for them then those applied for day mode, or is this even possible? Thank you!
Detecting and applying night mode CSS
I've been looking for a way to do this but I can't find the documentation for it, I assume it's impossible. The best you can do is force one of the two default style sheets like @Shiny said.

when in night mode class="dark" is on the body tag. class="light" is on the body tag in normal mode but you arguably don't need to worry about class="light" right now... maybe when it's not the default theme?

Try this CSS in stylish or something (change the username values to actual usernames on the page you're trying it on) and switch night mode on and off:

 [data-username="Atko"]:after,
 [data-username="PuttItOut"]:after{
 content: 'operator';
 margin:0 .25em 0 .5em;
 padding:2px 4px;
 border-radius:2px;
 border:1px solid hsla(0,100%,50%,.25);
 background:hsla(0,100%,90%,.25);
 color:hsla(0,100%,20%,1);
 }
 body.dark [data-username="Atko"]:after,
 body.dark [data-username="PuttItOut"]:after{
 background:hsla(0,20%,30%,1);
 color:hsla(0,100%,70%,1);
 }
